title: Member Protection Rule — Medical Certificates on Electric Service by Rate Schedule Accounts
content:
**Acceptance.** A medical certificate stating that a household member's health would be endangered by loss of service is accepted on an Electric Service by Rate Schedule account only where the schedule accepts medical certificates, and only when it is signed by a licensed physician, physician assistant or nurse practitioner. A certificate is accepted only when the number of certificates received on the same service account in the 365 days ending on the day before the received date of the certificate being considered is below the schedule's certificates per rolling 12 months.

**Protection.** An accepted certificate protects the account from disconnection through its expiry date, which is the received date plus the schedule's delay days, in calendar days, counted from the day after the received date.

**Effect on the balance.** The certificate postpones disconnection; it never forgives the balance, and late charges continue to apply.

**After disconnection.** A certificate received after the meter was disconnected does not by itself restore service; reconnection then follows the cooperative's reconnection conditions.

**Rejected for the renewal limit.** A certificate rejected for exceeding the renewal limit is recorded as received but does not update the protection date.

### Hypothetical dates (30 delay days)

| Received date | Protection through |
|---|---|
| June 5 | July 5 |
| January 20 | February 19 |

### Acceptance checklist applied to hypothetical certificates

| Schedule | Signed by | Certificates received in the prior 365 days (limit 2) | Accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Schedule R | Nurse practitioner | 1 | Yes |
| Schedule R | Physician | 2 | No — recorded as received, protection date unchanged |
| Schedule FH | Chiropractor | 0 | No — not a listed practitioner |
| Schedule GS-1 | Physician | 0 | No — the schedule accepts no certificate |
